claim: Activation of systemic acquired resistance in plants is associated with transcriptome reprogramming induced by the unstable coactivator NPR1.
source: Activation of systemic acquired resistance in plants is associated with transcriptome reprogramming induced by the unstable coactivator NPR1.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that draws from established knowledge about plant immunity and NPR1 function.

claim: Immune-induced ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of NPR1 are thought to facilitate continuous delivery of active NPR1 to target promoters, thereby maximising gene expression.
source: Immune-induced ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of NPR1 are thought to facilitate continuous delivery of active NPR1 to target promoters, thereby maximising gene expression.
evidence: This statement references a prevailing model in the field, supported by prior research.

claim: Ubiquitination of NPR1 is a progressive event in which initial modification by a Cullin-RING E3 ligase promotes its chromatin association and expression of target genes.
source: Here we show ubiquitination of NPR1 is a progressive event in which initial modification by a Cullin-RING E3 ligase promotes its chromatin association and expression of target genes.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: When polyubiquitination of NPR1 is enhanced by the E4 ligase UBE4, it is targeted for proteasomal degradation.
source: Only when polyubiquitination of NPR1 is enhanced by the E4 ligase, UBE4, it is targeted for proteasomal degradation.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing UBE4's role in NPR1 degradation.

claim: Ubiquitin ligase activities are opposed by UBP6/7, two proteasome-associated deubiquitinases that enhance NPR1 longevity.
source: Conversely, ubiquitin ligase activities are opposed by UBP6/7, two proteasome-associated deubiquitinases that enhance NPR1 longevity.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data on UBP6/7 function.

claim: Immune-induced transcriptome reprogramming requires sequential actions of E3 and E4 ligases balanced by opposing deubiquitinases that fine-tune activity of NPR1 without strict requirement for its sacrificial turnover.
source: Thus, immune-induced transcriptome reprogramming requires sequential actions of E3 and E4 ligases balanced by opposing deubiquitinases that fine-tune activity of NPR1 without strict requirement for its sacrificial turnover.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by multiple experimental findings.

claim: SA accumulates upon recognition of biotrophic pathogens in plants.
source: In plants transcriptional reprogramming is largely orchestrated by the immune hormone salicylic acid (SA) that accumulates upon recognition of biotrophic pathogens.
evidence: This is established knowledge in plant immunity research.

claim: SA is required for establishment of systemic acquired resistance (SAR).
source: SA not only induces resistance in infected local tissues, it is also required for establishment of systemic acquired resistance (SAR), a form of induced resistance with broad-spectrum effectiveness that is long-lasting and protects the entire plant from future pathogen attack (Spoel and Dong, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Establishment of SAR and associated transcriptome reprogramming are mediated by the transcriptional coactivator NPR1.
source: Establishment of SAR and associated transcriptome reprogramming are mediated by the transcriptional coactivator NPR1 (nonexpressor of pathogenesis-related (PR) genes 1).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by prior research.

claim: The majority of SA-induced genes are NPR1 dependent.
source: The majority of SA-induced genes are NPR1 dependent, indicating NPR1 is a master regulator of plant immunity (Wang et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Loss of NPR1 function results in severely immune-compromised plants unable to activate SAR.
source: Consequently, loss of NPR1 function results in severely immune-compromised plants unable to activate SAR.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research on NPR1 mutants.

claim: NPR1 exerts its activity in the nucleus.
source: Since NPR1 exerts its activity in the nucleus (Kinkema et al., 2000), controlling its nuclear entry provides a means to prevent spurious activation of immune responses.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: In resting cells NPR1 is sequestered in the cytoplasm as a large redox-sensitive oligomer formed by intermolecular disulphide linkages between conserved cysteine residues.
source: Indeed, in resting cells NPR1 is sequestered in the cytoplasm as a large redox-sensitive oligomer that is formed by intermolecular disulphide linkages between conserved cysteine residues (Mou et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: NPR1 monomers that escape oligomerization and enter the nucleus are ubiquitinated by a Cullin-RING Ligase 3 (CRL3), resulting in their degradation by the 26S proteasome.
source: NPR1 monomers that escape oligomerization and enter the nucleus are ubiquitinated by a Cullin-RING Ligase 3 (CRL3), a modular E3 ubiquitin ligase, resulting in their degradation by the 26S proteasome (Spoel et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Constitutive clearance of NPR1 from nuclei of resting cells by concerted action of CRL3 and the proteasome is necessary to prevent untimely activation of its target genes and associated autoimmunity.
source: Importantly, constitutive clearance of NPR1 from nuclei of resting cells by concerted action of CRL3 and the proteasome is necessary to prevent untimely activation of its target genes and associated autoimmunity.
evidence: This statement is supported by prior research on CRL3 function.

claim: Upon activation of SAR, NPR1 is subject to an array of post-translational modifications including alterations in redox-based modifications, phosphorylation and SUMOylation.
source: Upon activation of SAR, NPR1 is subject to an array of post-translational modifications. A combination of alterations in redox-based modifications, phosphorylation and SUMOylation of NPR1 result in the formation of a transactivation complex that induces the transcription of immune-responsive target genes (Skelly et al., 2016; Withers and Dong, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: NPR1 becomes phosphorylated at Ser11 and Ser15, which results in recruitment of CRL3 followed by its degradation.
source: Subsequent to these post-translational control points, NPR1 becomes phosphorylated at Ser11 and Ser15, which surprisingly results in recruitment of CRL3 followed by its degradation (Spoel et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of the proteasome, genetic mutation of CRL3, and mutation of Ser11/15 all stabilised NPR1 protein, yet impaired the expression of SA-induced NPR1 target genes.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of the proteasome, genetic mutation of CRL3, and mutation of Ser11/15 all stabilised NPR1 protein, yet impaired the expression of SA-induced NPR1 target genes (Spoel et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Ubiquitination and degradation of NPR1 are required for the full expression of its target genes.
source: These findings indicate that paradoxically, ubiquitination and degradation of NPR1 are required for the full expression of its target genes.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from prior research findings.

claim: SUMOylation of NPR1 was required for Ser11/15 phosphorylation and facilitates its interaction with other transcriptional activators.
source: SUMOylation of NPR1 was required for Ser11/15 phosphorylation and facilitates its interaction with other transcriptional activators (Saleh et al., 2015), suggesting that NPR1 becomes inactivated only after it has initiated gene transcription.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Transcriptional control by unstable (co)activators has been reported in other eukaryotes, including for key transcriptional regulators such as GCN4 in yeast and ERα, cMyc and SRC-3 activators in humans.
source: This type of transcriptional control by unstable (co)activators has also been reported in other eukaryotes, including for key transcriptional regulators such as the nutrient sensor GCN4 in yeast and the estrogen receptor ERα as well as oncogenic cMyc and SRC-3 activators in humans (Kim et al., 2003; Lipford et al., 2005; Métivier et al., 2003; Reid et al., 2003; von der Lehr et al., 2003; Wu et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The use of unstable transcriptional (co)activators may be an evolutionary conserved mechanism for fine-tuning gene expression.
source: This suggests that the use of unstable transcriptional (co)activators may be an evolutionary conserved mechanism for fine-tuning gene expression (Geng et al., 2012; Kodadek et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Chains of four or more ubiquitin molecules are thought to be necessary for recruitment of most substrates to the proteasome.
source: As chains of four or more ubiquitin molecules are thought to be necessary for recruitment of most substrates to the proteasome (Thrower et al., 2000), it is plausible that processive ubiquitination could provide a window of opportunity for NPR1 to activate its target genes.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Adult ube4 plants displayed enhanced expression of immune genes in absence of pathogen challenge.
source: Like mutants in CRL3 ligase that fail to degrade NPR1 (Spoel et al., 2009), adult ube4 plants displayed enhanced expression of immune genes in absence of pathogen challenge (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Adult ube4 mutants showed autoimmunity when challenged with a high inoculum of Psm ES4326.
source: In agreement with this, when the potential for enhanced disease resistance was examined by using a high inoculum of Psm ES4326, adult ube4 mutants showed autoimmunity (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The constitutive immune gene expression observed in ube4 was abolished in ube4 ics1 double mutant plants.
source: The constitutive immune gene expression observed in ube4 was abolished in ube4 ics1 double mutant plants (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The autoimmune phenotype of adult ube4 plants is completely dependent on SA.
source: In agreement with the gene expression data, enhanced susceptibility was maintained in ube4 ics1 double mutants (Figure 1D), indicating the autoimmune phenotype of adult ube4 plants is completely dependent on SA.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Constitutive immune gene expression in ube4 plants was abolished in ube4 npr1 plants.
source: Constitutive immune gene expression in ube4 plants was abolished in ube4 npr1 plants (Figure 1E) and this double mutant was equally susceptible to a low Psm ES4326 inoculum as npr1 single mutants (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1E and 1F.

claim: In unchallenged plants UBE4 suppresses the expression of SA-mediated NPR1 target genes and prevents autoimmunity.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that in unchallenged plants UBE4 suppresses the expression of SA-mediated NPR1 target genes and prevents autoimmunity, conceivably by altering the stability of upstream NLR immune receptors as well as the downstream NPR1 coactivator.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings.

claim: YFP-UBE4 fusion protein is partly localised to the nucleus.
source: Expression of a YFP-UBE4 fusion protein in Arabidopsis protoplasts confirmed it is indeed partly localised to the nucleus (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Both SA-induced constitutively expressed NPR1-GFP and endogenous NPR1 from WT plants were degraded within a few hours after exposure to cycloheximide.
source: Both SA-induced constitutively expressed NPR1-GFP (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) (Kinkema et al., 2000) and endogenous NPR1 from WT plants were degraded within a few hours after exposure to cycloheximide (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2A, 2B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Both NPR1-GFP and endogenous NPR1 were considerably more stable in the ube4 mutant genetic background.
source: By contrast, both proteins were considerably more stable in the ube4 mutant genetic background.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: UBE4 promotes NPR1 degradation.
source: Taken together these results indicate that UBE4 promotes NPR1 degradation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings.

claim: Ser11/15 phosphorylation of NPR1-GFP was unaffected by the ube4 mutation.
source: However, Ser11/15 phosphorylation of NPR1-GFP was unaffected by the ube4 mutation (Figure 2C), indicating UBE4 mediates NPR1 turnover downstream of CRL3-mediated ubiquitination.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: UBE4 mediates NPR1 turnover downstream of CRL3-mediated ubiquitination.
source: However, Ser11/15 phosphorylation of NPR1-GFP was unaffected by the ube4 mutation (Figure 2C), indicating UBE4 mediates NPR1 turnover downstream of CRL3-mediated ubiquitination.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: SA stimulated polyubiquitination of NPR1-GFP.
source: Pulldown of polyubiquitinated proteins using tandem-repeated ubiquitin-binding entities (TUBE) (Hjerpe et al., 2009) followed by detection of NPR1-GFP, revealed that SA stimulated polyubiquitination of NPR1-GFP (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: SA-induced polyubiquitination of NPR1-GFP was compromised in ube4 mutants.
source: By contrast, SA-induced polyubiquitination of NPR1-GFP was compromised in ube4 mutants (Figure 2D), but ubiquitinated NPR1 was still detected at high-molecular weight.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The amount of SA-induced polyubiquitinated NPR1-GFP pulled down with recombinant S5aUIM was strikingly lower in ube4 mutants compared to plants carrying wild-type UBE4 alleles.
source: Compared to plants carrying wild-type UBE4 alleles, the amount of SA-induced polyubiquitinated NPR1-GFP pulled down with recombinant S5aUIM was strikingly lower in ube4 mutants (Figure 2E), indicating that UBE4 promotes formation of long ubiquitin chains on NPR1 leading to its proteasomal degradation.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: UBE4 promotes formation of long ubiquitin chains on NPR1 leading to its proteasomal degradation.
source: Compared to plants carrying wild-type UBE4 alleles, the amount of SA-induced polyubiquitinated NPR1-GFP pulled down with recombinant S5aUIM was strikingly lower in ube4 mutants (Figure 2E), indicating that UBE4 promotes formation of long ubiquitin chains on NPR1 leading to its proteasomal degradation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: NPR1-GFP specifically pulled down FLAG-UBE4.
source: As shown in Figure 2F, NPR1-GFP specifically pulled down FLAG-UBE4, indicating that UBE4 physically binds to polyubiquitinated NPR1 to facilitate ubiquitin chain extension.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: UBE4 physically binds to polyubiquitinated NPR1 to facilitate ubiquitin chain extension.
source: As shown in Figure 2F, NPR1-GFP specifically pulled down FLAG-UBE4, indicating that UBE4 physically binds to polyubiquitinated NPR1 to facilitate ubiquitin chain extension.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Plants carrying two different ube4 mutant alleles exhibited elevated expression levels of NPR1 target genes that were much higher than in WT.
source: In stark contrast to cul3a cul3b mutants that were compromised in SA-induced expression of NPR1 target genes, plants carrying two different ube4 mutant alleles exhibited elevated expression levels that were much higher than in WT (Figure 3A and B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3A, 3B, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Among 2612 genes whose expression changed by ≥2 fold in response to SA in WT or ube4 mutants, 75% were stringently dependent on NPR1.
source: Among 2612 genes whose expression changed by ≥2 fold in response to SA in WT or ube4 mutants, 75% were stringently dependent on NPR1 (i.e. ≥1.5 fold difference compared to npr1) (Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding from RNA-Seq analysis.

claim: The majority of SA-induced genes received a boost in expression when UBE4 was knocked out.
source: The majority of SA-induced genes in category 1, including PR1 and WRKY marker genes, received a boost in expression when UBE4 was knocked out (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: SA-regulated genes that were not dependent on NPR1 behaved similarly in WT and mutant ube4 plants.
source: By contrast, SA-regulated genes that were not dependent on NPR1 behaved similarly in WT and mutant ube4 plants (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), suggesting UBE4 exerts its effects predominantly through NPR1.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: UBE4 exerts its effects predominantly through NPR1.
source: By contrast, SA-regulated genes that were not dependent on NPR1 behaved similarly in WT and mutant ube4 plants (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), suggesting UBE4 exerts its effects predominantly through NPR1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In absence of UBE4-mediated long-chain polyubiquitination, NPR1 remains in a highly active transcriptional state.
source: Together these data suggest that in absence of UBE4-mediated long-chain polyubiquitination, NPR1 remains in a highly active transcriptional state.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings.

claim: SA-induced NPR1 accumulated to elevated levels in both cul3a/b and ube4 mutants compared to WT plants.
source: Compared to WT plants, SA-induced NPR1 accumulated to elevated levels in both cul3a/b and ube4 mutants (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: At 8 hr after SA treatment more NPR1-GFP was bound to the PR1 promoter in ube4 mutants compared to plants carrying wild-type UBE4 alleles.
source: Coinciding with elevated PR1 gene expression, at 8 hr after SA treatment more NPR1-GFP was bound to the PR1 promoter in ube4 mutants compared to plants carrying wild-type UBE4 alleles (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: In absence of long polyubiquitin chains, early occupancy by transcriptionally competent NPR1 is increased at target promoters.
source: This indicates that in absence of long polyubiquitin chains, early occupancy by transcriptionally competent NPR1 is increased at target promoters.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from ChIP data.

claim: At 24 hr after SA treatment, NPR1-GFP was still associated with the PR1 promoter in plants expressing wild-type UBE4, but not in ube4 mutants.
source: We also examined a later time point after SA treatment (24 hr) and found that NPR1-GFP was still associated with the PR1 promoter in plants expressing wild-type UBE4, but not in ube4 mutants (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: In absence of long-chain polyubiquitination NPR1 strongly switches on target genes without the need for long-term residency at their promoters.
source: Nonetheless, PR1 gene expression remained at elevated levels in these mutants (Figure 3G), implying that in absence of long-chain polyubiquitination NPR1 strongly switches on target genes without the need for long-term residency at their promoters.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from ChIP and gene expression data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: cul3a cul3b ube4 mutants showed severe developmental defects, including stunted growth and complete sterility.
source: Strikingly, cul3a cul3b ube4 mutants showed severe developmental defects, including stunted growth and complete sterility (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is a primary observation supported by images shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: In cul3a cul3b ube4 mutants the SA-induced expression of several genes was impaired to a similar extend as in cul3a cul3b double mutants.
source: In cul3a cul3b ube4 mutants the SA-induced expression of several genes, including PR genes, was impaired to a similar extend as in cul3a cul3b double mutants, indicating that elevated gene expression observed in ube4 plants is dependent on CRL3 (Figure 3H and I).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3H and 3I.

claim: Elevated gene expression observed in ube4 plants is dependent on CRL3.
source: In cul3a cul3b ube4 mutants the SA-induced expression of several genes, including PR genes, was impaired to a similar extend as in cul3a cul3b double mutants, indicating that elevated gene expression observed in ube4 plants is dependent on CRL3 (Figure 3H and I).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figures 3H and 3I.

claim: A subset of NPR1 target genes (WRKY18, WRKY38, WRKY62) were dramatically upregulated in cul3a cul3b ube4 mutants to a level higher than in any of the other genotypes.
source: However, a subset of NPR1 target genes (i.e. WRKY18, WRKY38, WRKY62) were dramatically upregulated in cul3a cul3b ube4 mutants to a level higher than in any of the other genotypes.
evidence: This is a primary finding from gene expression analysis.

claim: CRL3 and UBE4 function sequentially in the stepwise addition or extension of ubiquitin chains on NPR1 but with opposing effects on its transcriptional activity.
source: Regardless of this specific, our broader findings suggest that CRL3 and UBE4 function sequentially in the stepwise addition or extension of ubiquitin chains on NPR1 but with opposing effects on its transcriptional activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings.

claim: SA-induced PR1 and WRKY gene expression was inhibited by increasing concentrations of MG132 in NPR1-GFP (in npr1) plants.
source: SA-induced PR1 and WRKY gene expression was inhibited by increasing concentrations of MG132 in NPR1-GFP (in npr1) plants (Figure 3J and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3J and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The SA-induced expression of NPR1 target genes was largely unresponsive to MG132 in ube4 mutants.
source: By contrast, the SA-induced expression of these NPR1 target genes was largely unresponsive to MG132 in ube4 mutants, especially at lower concentrations.
evidence: This is a primary finding from gene expression analysis.

claim: Loss of UBE4 largely uncoupled NPR1 target gene expression from proteasome activity.
source: Thus, loss of UBE4 largely uncoupled NPR1 target gene expression from proteasome activity, demonstrating the importance of progressive ubiquitination for NPR1 activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data on MG132 treatment.

claim: Initial CRL3-mediated ubiquitination is required for NPR1 to attain its full transcriptional activity.
source: In summary, our findings indicate that initial CRL3-mediated ubiquitination is required for NPR1 to attain its full transcriptional activity, while the stepwise formation of long ubiquitin chains mediated by UBE4 inactivates NPR1 and promotes its degradation by the proteasome.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings.

claim: The stepwise formation of long ubiquitin chains mediated by UBE4 inactivates NPR1 and promotes its degradation by the proteasome.
source: In summary, our findings indicate that initial CRL3-mediated ubiquitination is required for NPR1 to attain its full transcriptional activity, while the stepwise formation of long ubiquitin chains mediated by UBE4 inactivates NPR1 and promotes its degradation by the proteasome.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings.

claim: The broad-spectrum inhibitors PR-619 and NSC632839 strongly impaired SA-induced gene expression across all NPR1 target genes tested.
source: The broad-spectrum inhibitors PR-619 (Altun et al., 2011) and NSC632839 (Aleo et al., 2006) strongly impaired SA-induced gene expression across all NPR1 target genes tested (Figure 4A), suggesting that DUB activity is required for their optimal expression.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: DUB activity is required for optimal expression of NPR1 target genes.
source: The broad-spectrum inhibitors PR-619 (Altun et al., 2011) and NSC632839 (Aleo et al., 2006) strongly impaired SA-induced gene expression across all NPR1 target genes tested (Figure 4A), suggesting that DUB activity is required for their optimal expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Treatment with PR-619 or NSC632839 did not affect SA-induced transcription of the NPR1 gene, but depleted NPR1 protein levels.
source: Furthermore, while treatment with PR-619 or NSC632839 did not affect SA-induced transcription of the NPR1 gene, it depleted NPR1 protein levels (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: DUB activity may be required for NPR1-dependent gene expression and for increasing NPR1 stability.
source: Thus, DUB activity may not only be required for NPR1-dependent gene expression but also for increasing NPR1 stability.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data on DUB inhibitor effects.

claim: NSC632839 and MG132 treatments dramatically enhanced accumulation of ubiquitin conjugates, especially in combination with SA treatment.
source: While NSC632839 and MG132 treatments dramatically enhanced accumulation of ubiquitin conjugates, especially in combination with SA treatment, all other inhibitors had little effect on cellular ubiquitination levels (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: All tested DUB inhibitors strongly suppressed SA-induced expression of NPR1 target genes.
source: We then examined the effect of these DUB inhibitors on SA-induced gene expression. All inhibitors strongly suppressed SA-induced expression of NPR1 target genes (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Most DUB inhibitors were effective at low micromolar concentrations and suppressed NPR1 target genes in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Furthermore, most inhibitors were effective at low micromolar concentrations and suppressed NPR1 target genes in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: DUB activity may be crucial for NPR1 stability and efficient activation of SA-induced NPR1 target genes.
source: Collectively these data provide a first indication that DUB activity may be crucial for NPR1 stability and efficient activation of SA-induced NPR1 target genes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings with DUB inhibitors.

claim: SA-induced PR1 and WRKY gene expression was generally comparable between uch3 and WT plants.
source: Figure 5A shows that SA-induced PR1 and WRKY gene expression was generally comparable between uch3 and WT plants, indicating UCH3 is unlikely to play a major role.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: UCH3 is unlikely to play a major role in SA-induced gene expression.
source: Figure 5A shows that SA-induced PR1 and WRKY gene expression was generally comparable between uch3 and WT plants, indicating UCH3 is unlikely to play a major role.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: ubp12-2w plants exhibited elevated PR1 expression but other NPR1 target genes were activated to a slightly lesser extent as in WT.
source: Similar to a previous report (Ewan et al., 2011), we observed elevated PR1 expression in ubp12-2w plants but other NPR1 target genes were activated to a slightly lesser extent as in WT (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: SA-induced expression of PR1 was slightly lower in ubp6 and ubp7 single mutants but WRKY gene expression was largely comparable to WT plants.
source: SA-induced expression of PR1 was slightly lower in these mutants but WRKY gene expression was largely comparable to WT plants (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: ubp6 ubp7 mutants were impaired in activation of SA-induced gene expression.
source: However, ubp6 ubp7 mutants were impaired in activation of SA-induced gene expression (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: UBP6 and UBP7 are functionally redundant and required for NPR1 target gene expression.
source: This indicates that UBP6 and UBP7 are functionally redundant and required for NPR1 target gene expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data on ubp6 ubp7 double mutants.

claim: The proteasomal subunits S5a and RPN6 both co-immunoprecipitated with FLAG-tagged UBP6.
source: The proteasomal subunits S5a and RPN6 both co-immunoprecipitated with FLAG-tagged UBP6 (Figure 6A), indicating UBP6 is also a proteasome-associated DUB in plants.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: UBP6 is a proteasome-associated DUB in plants.
source: The proteasomal subunits S5a and RPN6 both co-immunoprecipitated with FLAG-tagged UBP6 (Figure 6A), indicating UBP6 is also a proteasome-associated DUB in plants.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: HA-UbVS readily labelled T7-UBP6 but only upon addition of 26S proteasomes.
source: HA-UbVS readily labelled T7-UBP6 but only upon addition of 26S proteasomes (Figure 6B), indicating UBP6 has proteasome-activated DUB activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: UBP6 has proteasome-activated DUB activity.
source: HA-UbVS readily labelled T7-UBP6 but only upon addition of 26S proteasomes (Figure 6B), indicating UBP6 has proteasome-activated DUB activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Addition of WP1130 inhibitor completely blocked HA-UbVS labelling of UBP6.
source: Moreover, addition of WP1130 inhibitor completely blocked HA-UbVS labelling (Figure 6B), illustrating the effectiveness of this inhibitor on Arabidopsis UBP6.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Arabidopsis UBP6 displayed very little deubiquitination activity on free ubiquitin chains or di-ubiquitin of K48 and K63 linkage types.
source: Similar to human USP14, Arabidopsis UBP6 displayed very little deubiquitination activity on free ubiquitin chains or di-ubiquitin of K48 and K63 linkage types (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–1C.

claim: Wild-type UBP6 but not UBP6(C113S) was weakly capable of trimming K63-linked chains in presence of 26S proteasomes.
source: Only wild-type UBP6 but not UBP6(C113S) in which the catalytic cysteine residue was mutated, was weakly capable of trimming K63-linked chains in presence of 26S proteasomes, although this activity required very long incubation times (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Incubation of purified polyubiquitinated NPR1-GFP with recombinant UBP6 and 26S proteasomes led to the release of ubiquitin conjugates of approximately hexa-ubiquitin chain length.
source: Indeed, incubation of purified polyubiquitinated NPR1-GFP with recombinant UBP6 and 26S proteasomes led to the release of ubiquitin conjugates of approximately hexa-ubiquitin chain length (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Release of ubiquitin conjugates from NPR1 by UBP6 was dependent on SA treatment.
source: This release of ubiquitin conjugates was dependent on SA treatment, suggesting that UBP6 counteracts SA-induced polyubiquitination of NPR1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: UBP6 is an active DUB capable of removing ubiquitin chains en bloc from NPR1.
source: Together, these results demonstrate that UBP6 is an active DUB capable of removing ubiquitin chains en bloc from NPR1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings.

claim: Treatment of NPR1-GFP seedlings with WP1130 inhibitor increased the levels of SA-induced polyubiquitinated NPR1-GFP while reducing the unmodified amount of this protein.
source: We found that treatment of NPR1-GFP (in npr1) seedlings with WP1130 inhibitor increased the levels of SA-induced polyubiquitinated NPR1-GFP while reducing the unmodified amount of this protein (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: UBP6 and UBP7 activities are required for deubiquitination of SA-induced NPR1-GFP, thereby rescuing it from degradation.
source: This suggests that UBP6 and UBP7 activities are required for deubiquitination of SA-induced NPR1-GFP, thereby rescuing it from degradation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data on WP1130 treatment.

claim: Compared to WT plants, NPR1 was destabilised in ubp6 ubp7 mutants.
source: CHX chase experiments revealed that compared to WT plants, NPR1 was destabilised in ubp6 ubp7 mutants (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Expression of FLAG-tagged UBP6 in the ubp6/7 mutant background restored NPR1 stability.
source: Accordingly, expression of FLAG-tagged UBP6 in the ubp6/7 mutant background restored NPR1 stability (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

claim: UBP6 and UBP7 serve to stabilise NPR1 by removing ubiquitin chains that signal for its proteasome-mediated degradation.
source: These results demonstrate that UBP6 and UBP7 serve to stabilise NPR1 by removing ubiquitin chains that signal for its proteasome-mediated degradation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings.

claim: SA-induced association of NPR1-GFP with the PR1 promoter was strongly enhanced in presence of WP1130 inhibitor.
source: Surprisingly, ChIP experiments showed that SA-induced association of NPR1-GFP with the PR1 promoter was strongly enhanced in presence of WP1130 inhibitor (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: UBP6 and UBP7 prevent the build-up of long polyubiquitin chains that block the transcriptional activity of NPR1.
source: This suggests that UBP6 and UBP7 prevent the build-up of long polyubiquitin chains that block the transcriptional activity of NPR1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from ChIP data.

claim: UBP6 and UBP7 exhibit proteasome inhibitory activity.
source: It also implies that similar to their yeast homologue, UBP6 and UBP7 exhibit proteasome inhibitory activity (Hanna et al., 2006).
evidence: This is an inference based on similarity to yeast homologues and supported by a citation.

claim: Expression of FLAG-UBP6 fully restored SA-responsiveness in ubp6 ubp7 mutants.
source: While ubp6 ubp7 mutants were compromised in SA-induced activation of all NPR1 target genes tested, expression of FLAG-UBP6 fully restored SA-responsiveness (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: FLAG-UBP6m restored SA-induced expression of only a subset, but not all NPR1 target genes.
source: By contrast, FLAG-UBP6m restored SA-induced expression of only a subset, but not all NPR1 target genes.
evidence: This is a primary finding from gene expression analysis.

claim: A distinction was observed between WRKY and PR genes, with the former requiring catalytic DUB activity of UBP6 while the latter did not.
source: A distinction was observed between WRKY and PR genes, with the former requiring catalytic DUB activity of UBP6 while the latter did not (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Catalytic and non-catalytic activities of UBP6 regulate distinct NPR1-dependent gene sets.
source: These data indicate that catalytic and non-catalytic activities of UBP6 regulate distinct NPR1-dependent gene sets.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data on UBP6 complementation.

claim: SA treatment induced resistance in WT plants but did not block bacterial propagation in ubp6/7 plants.
source: SA treatment induced resistance in WT plants but did not block bacterial propagation in ubp6/7 plants (Figure 6H).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by pathogen infection data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: UBP6 and UBP7 are required for NPR1 coactivator activity and associated development of SA-dependent immunity.
source: Collectively, these data clearly demonstrate that UBP6 and UBP7 are required for NPR1 coactivator activity and associated development of SA-dependent immunity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings.

claim: Transcription-coupled degradation of unstable (co)activators is an energy-expensive process.
source: However, this sacrificial process is energy-expensive (Collins and Goldberg, 2017; Peth et al., 2013), raising a dilemma of why such mechanisms evolved to regulate transcriptional activators.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Ubiquitin chain extension and trimming activities can fine-tune transcriptional outputs of unstable eukaryotic activators without strict requirement for sacrificial turnover.
source: Our study on the immune coactivator NPR1, however, indicates that ubiquitin chain extension and trimming activities can fine-tune transcriptional outputs of unstable eukaryotic activators without strict requirement for sacrificial turnover.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by multiple experimental findings.

claim: In resting cells, CRL3-mediated turnover of NPR1 is important for preventing autoimmunity in absence of pathogen threat.
source: In resting cells, CRL3-mediated turnover of NPR1 is important for preventing autoimmunity in absence of pathogen threat (Spoel et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: E4 ligases are thought to extend existing ubiquitin chains rather than initiating substrate ubiquitination.
source: Rather than initiating substrate ubiquitination, E4 ligases are thought to extend existing ubiquitin chains (Crosas et al., 2006; Koegl et al., 1999), thereby determining substrate commitment to proteasome-mediated degradation and contributing to proteasome processivity (Aviram and Kornitzer, 2010; Koegl et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Arabidopsis UBE4/MUSE3 works in concert with a CRL1/SCFCPR1 ligase to regulate stability of the intercellular immune receptors SNC1 and RPS2.
source: Arabidopsis UBE4/MUSE3 works in concert with a CRL1/SCFCPR1 ligase to regulate stability of the intercellular immune receptors SNC1 and RPS2 that recognise pathogen invasion (Cheng et al., 2011; Gou et al., 2012; Huang et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: A single E4 enzyme may assist in diverse ubiquitin-mediated pathways controlled by different E3 ligases.
source: Taken together with our finding that UBE4 acts in concert with CRL3 (Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1), this suggests a single E4 enzyme may assist in diverse ubiquitin-mediated pathways controlled by different E3 ligases.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data and prior research.

claim: The stability of p53 is regulated by the E3 ligase MDM2.
source: The stability of p53 is regulated by amongst others the E3 ligase MDM2 (or HDM2 in humans) (Pant and Lozano, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: MDM2 only catalyses multi-monoubiquitination of p53, which is insufficient for recognition by the proteasome.
source: Although MDM2 limits p53 activity by promoting its turnover, MDM2 only catalyses multi-monoubiquitination of p53, which is insufficient for recognition by the proteasome (Lai et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Progression to the polyubiquitinated form of p53 in the nucleus is carried out by the U-box E4 ligase UBE4B.
source: Progression to the polyubiquitinated form of p53 in the nucleus is carried out by the U-box E4 ligase UBE4B that interacts with both MDM2 and p53 (Li et al., 2003; Wu and Leng, 2011; Wu et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: MDM2-mediated monoubiquitination controls nucleocytoplasmic trafficking of p53.
source: While MDM2-mediated monoubiquitination controls nucleocytoplasmic trafficking of p53 (Li et al., 2003), it probably does not have a direct effect on intrinsic p53 activator activity.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Progression to polyubiquitin chain formation by UBE4 results in transcriptional shut down as polyubiquitinated NPR1 still occupied target promoters but lacked transcriptional potency.
source: Although it remains unclear if CRL3 adds only monoubiquitin or generates short chains shy of tetraubiquitin, the minimal signal required for proteasome recognition (Thrower et al., 2000), progression to polyubiquitin chain formation by UBE4 results in transcriptional shut down as polyubiquitinated NPR1 still occupied target promoters but lacked transcriptional potency (Figure 6D and F).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figures 6D and 6F.

claim: Stepwise ubiquitination may be a general mechanism to control unstable transcriptional (co)activators in eukaryotes.
source: This type of stepwise ubiquitination may be a general mechanism to control unstable transcriptional (co)activators in eukaryotes.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the findings of the study.

claim: Multi-monoubiquitination of the oncogenic growth coactivator SRC-3 results in its transcriptional activation, while subsequent chain extension targets it for degradation.
source: For example, multi-monoubiquitination of the oncogenic growth coactivator SRC-3 results in its transcriptional activation, while subsequent chain extension targets it for degradation, but E4 ligases have not yet been implicated.
evidence: This statement draws from established knowledge about SRC-3 regulation.

claim: Stepwise ubiquitination established by the sequential actions of E3 and E4 ligases may generate a transcriptional timer that controls the activity and lifetime of unstable (co)activators.
source: We propose here that stepwise ubiquitination established by the sequential actions of E3 and E4 ligases may generate a transcriptional timer that controls the activity and lifetime of unstable (co)activators (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the findings of the study, illustrated in Figure 7.

claim: Several unstable mammalian transcription activators, including p53 and NF-κB, are regulated by diverse DUBs.
source: Several unstable mammalian transcription activators, including p53 and the immune activator NF-κB, are also regulated by diverse DUBs (Colleran et al., 2013; Pant and Lozano, 2014; Schweitzer and Naumann, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Loss of USP7-mediated deubiquitination of NF-κB resulted in increased turnover and decreased promoter occupancy of NF-κB.
source: For example, loss of USP7-mediated deubiquitination of NF-κB resulted in increased turnover and decreased promoter occupancy of NF-κB (Colleran et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Knockout of UBP6 and UBP7 resulted in enhanced turnover and decreased transcriptional output of NPR1.
source: Similarly, we found that knockout of UBP6 and UBP7 resulted in enhanced turnover and decreased transcriptional output of NPR1 (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: UBP6 showed a similar DUB activity as its mammalian homologue USP14, in that it appeared to deubiquitinate NPR1 by removing ubiquitin chains en bloc.
source: UBP6 showed a similar DUB activity as its mammalian homologue USP14 (Lee et al., 2016), in that it appeared to deubiquitinate NPR1 by removing ubiquitin chains en bloc (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figures 6C and 6D, supported by a citation.

claim: In yeast Ubp6 was previously reported to oppose ubiquitin chain extension activity of the E4 ligase Hul5, thereby regulating substrate recruitment to the proteasome.
source: In yeast Ubp6 was previously reported to oppose ubiquitin chain extension activity of the E4 ligase Hul5, thereby regulating substrate recruitment to the proteasome (Crosas et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Arabidopsis UBP6 and UBP7 opposed ubiquitin ligase activities to extend the lifetime of transcriptionally active NPR1.
source: Similarly, Arabidopsis UBP6 and UBP7 opposed ubiquitin ligase activities to extend the lifetime of transcriptionally active NPR1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings.

claim: All tested DUB inhibitors blocked NPR1 target gene expression, while mutation of exclusively UBP6 and UBP7 had a similar effect.
source: This is illustrated by our findings that all tested DUB inhibitors blocked NPR1 target gene expression, while mutation of exclusively UBP6 and UBP7 had a similar effect.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings.

claim: The specificity of DUB inhibitors has well-recognised limitations in that they often target multiple related DUBs.
source: This discrepancy is expected because the specificity of DUB inhibitors has well-recognised limitations in that they often target multiple related DUBs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is established knowledge about DUB inhibitor limitations.

claim: Disparate ubiquitin modifying enzymes play important roles in establishment of plant immune responses.
source: In summary, we report that disparate ubiquitin modifying enzymes play important roles in establishment of plant immune responses.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion of the study.

claim: The opposing actions of an E3 and E4 ligase pair and two DUBs can fine-tune transcriptional outputs of the unstable immune coactivator NPR1 without strict requirement for its sacrificial turnover.
source: We demonstrate that the opposing actions of an E3 and E4 ligase pair and two DUBs can fine-tune transcriptional outputs of the unstable immune coactivator NPR1 without strict requirement for its sacrificial turnover.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by multiple experimental findings.

claim: Dynamicity in conjugated ubiquitin chain length may be a powerful mechanism for controlling the activity of unstable eukaryotic (co)activators in general.
source: Dynamicity in conjugated ubiquitin chain length may be a powerful mechanism for controlling the activity of unstable eukaryotic (co)activators in general.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the findings of the study.
